served.stem: The author's handling of the two awareness figures in paragraph 13 is best described as
choices: confident that the lower figure is the accurate one
convinced that the higher figure proves patients are routinely awake and aware during surgery
impatient with colleagues who keep raising the question
certain that the difference is a simple error of record keeping
deliberate about leaving the disagreement open and treating the gap as informative
served.bankWhy: Paragraph 13 gives both numbers, says honest disagreement about the question runs through the literature, and then calls the distance between the two figures a finding in its own right.

The distance between those two figures is itself a finding.

passage.title: Why Anaesthesia Still Lacks an Explanation

distractorNotes: Both numbers are given without either being endorsed, and the disagreement is called honest.
Almost none of the patients who respond remember anything, and the author declines to say what that amounts to.
No irritation toward anyone appears here. The open question is presented as worth having.
The gap is called a finding, which makes it informative rather than a mistake in the records.

answer.line: Paragraph 13 gives both figures, calls the disagreement honest, and says the distance between them is itself a finding.

steps: Find the two figures: paragraph 13, sentence 4. One in twenty thousand when patients volunteer it, twenty or thirty times higher when every patient is asked.
Read what the author does with them: "The distance between those two figures is itself a finding."
Sentence 3 calls the debate over whether a patient who squeezes on command is conscious an "honest disagreement". No side is picked.

choices.text: confident that the lower figure is the accurate one
choices.note: The author endorses neither number. The gap between them is the point.

choices.text: convinced that the higher figure proves patients are routinely awake and aware during surgery
choices.note: Even the higher figure is a small minority, and almost none of the patients who squeeze on command remember anything.

choices.text: impatient with colleagues who keep raising the question
choices.note: The author calls the disagreement honest. That is respect for the question, not irritation.

choices.text: certain that the difference is a simple error of record keeping
choices.note: Sentence 5 calls the distance between the figures a finding. A finding is information, not a record-keeping slip.

choices.text: deliberate about leaving the disagreement open and treating the gap as informative
choices.note: Both figures kept, the disagreement called honest, the gap called a finding: open on purpose.

student.lockIt: When an author refuses to pick a side and says why, that refusal is the attitude.
